reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a crypto bot project promising a 1.5% daily return and recovery of the initial investment after 15 days. The presenter demonstrates connecting a wallet and depositing $50, then directs interested viewers to use a referral link, while the interface shows funding, profit-claim, and tiered invitation features. The video also notes that the claims may be made up and that the project has an unidentified team and unaudited contracts.

opening.argument: Judge, the presenter does not ask viewers to trust this project. The description says he is not telling anyone to follow him, and he advises anyone considering it to use risk capital only. He also questions whether the project's history is real and says he cannot readily check it. Those warnings matter more than his interest in the idea: he is showing a risky project while openly identifying reasons to doubt it.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited 15-day withdrawal statement describes a claimed option, not proof that withdrawal succeeds. Nor does the $50 wallet demonstration erase his explicit uncertainty. Even when discussing the unaudited contracts, he says he is uncomfortable with that fact. The referral mention deserves scrutiny, but it does not make his repeated warnings disappear.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The warnings are real, but they do not turn the video into a warning-first examination. The presenter makes a deposit, tells interested viewers he will provide his referral link, and asks them to use it. Risk language does not undo that direct invitation to participate in a project he presents as offering daily returns.

opening.argument: Judge, much of the presentation walks through how the proposed technology and interface are described. The presenter explains the mempool, points viewers toward Ethereum developer documentation, and shows how to limit a token's spend permission before depositing. His small deposit functions as a live test whose results he says he will report later; the video does not show that the bots delivered returns. Read this as an operational walkthrough with an unresolved outcome, not a certification of the service.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening quotes about bots describe the proposed mechanism, not independently verified profits. The deposit shows what the presenter did, not what a viewer should expect to earn. He even notes that the displayed bot figures are measured from inception, a qualification the return-focused reading leaves out. A walkthrough can examine striking claims without validating them.

The presenter says the bot platform is 'completely different,' demonstrates funding it, and offers his referral link to viewers who want to join. A pending personal update cannot verify the advertised return at the point when viewers are invited to deposit.

opening.argument: Judge, the evidence supports a narrower reading than a proven scam mechanism. The site describes a bot service and a way to share funds with it; the presenter uses his own wallet for a $50 trial. The stated 1.5% is an average, and the quoted explanation expressly allows for losing days. A referral link is present, but the record does not show referral earnings being paid or a viewer earning a return. These are reasons to assess the service cautiously, not to treat its claimed outcome as established.

rebuttal.rebuttal: A five-level referral feature shows an incentive to invite others, but the quoted line alone does not establish what anyone was paid. Likewise, 'You can get your initial investment back after 15 days' is a claim about the service, not evidence of a successful withdrawal or a guaranteed return. The presenter expressly acknowledges that the operators may be untrustworthy; the case should not convert unverified claims into verified outcomes.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A completed payout is not needed to identify what the video promotes. The presenter describes a daily-return offer, funds it on camera, and asks interested viewers to use his referral link. Calling the rate an average leaves the central offer intact. He also says the team is not identified and the contracts lack an audit, so the video supplies no independent basis for trusting the claimed bot profits.
